title.zh: 卷七十八 志第二十八: 輿服一
title.raw: 卷七十八 志第二十八: 輿服一 Volume 78 Treatises 31: Carriages and Clothes 1

sentences.zh: 輿服一

translations.literal: Carriages and Clothes 1
translations.idiomatic: Carriages and Clothes, Part One

sentences.zh: 〈（儀衛附）〉

translations.literal: (Ceremonial Escort appended.)
translations.idiomatic: The gloss notes that Ceremonial Escort is appended at the end.〉

sentences.zh: 若稽往古，黃帝、堯、舜垂衣裳而天下治，蓋取諸乾坤；

translations.literal: If one examines antiquity, the Yellow Emperor, Yao, and Shun let their robes hang down and the realm was well governed—this was taken from Qian and Kun;
translations.idiomatic: Looking back to antiquity, the Yellow Emperor, Yao, and Shun governed the realm simply by letting their robes hang at ease, drawing this pattern from the hexagrams Qian and Kun;

sentences.zh: 服牛乘馬，引重致遠，蓋取諸大壯。

translations.literal: They harnessed oxen and rode horses, drawing heavy loads and reaching far distances—this was taken from Da Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: They put oxen to the yoke and rode horses to haul heavy burdens over long distances, taking this model from the hexagram Da Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 冕服車輿之制，其來尚矣。

translations.literal: The institutions of ceremonial caps and robes and of carriages and chariots have been esteemed since long ago.
translations.idiomatic: The regulations governing ceremonial dress and state carriages reach back to a very remote antiquity.

sentences.zh: 《虞書》舜作十二章，五服以命有德，車服以賞有功。

translations.literal: The 《Documents of Yu》 records that Shun made the twelve emblems; the five grades of dress were used to appoint the virtuous, and carriage regalia to reward the meritorious.
translations.idiomatic: The 《Documents of Yu》 records that Shun devised the twelve emblem patterns, using the five grades of dress to invest the worthy and carriage regalia to reward merit.

sentences.zh: 《禮記》虞鸞車，夏鉤車，商大輅。

translations.literal: The 《Record of Rites》: Yu had the luan carriage, Xia the gou carriage, and Shang the great lu.
translations.idiomatic: The 《Record of Rites》 notes that Yu used the luan carriage, Xia the gou carriage, and Shang the great state carriage.

sentences.zh: 至周，損益前代，弁師掌王之五冕，巾車掌王之五輅，而儀文始備。

translations.literal: By the Zhou, they reduced and augmented the former ages; the cap master supervised the king's five caps, the carriage master the king's five carriages, and ritual forms were first complete.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhou, earlier institutions were revised as needed; the cap master oversaw the king's five ceremonial caps and the carriage master the five state carriages, and only then did ritual protocol become fully established.

sentences.zh: 然孔子論治天下之大法，於殷輅取其質而得中，周冕取其文而得中也。

translations.literal: Yet when Confucius discussed the great method of governing the realm, of the Yin carriage he took its substance and attained the mean; of the Zhou cap he took its ornament and attained the mean.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in discussing the great principles of governing the realm, Confucius praised the Yin carriage for its plain substance as hitting the mean, and the Zhou cap for its refined ornament as likewise attaining the mean.

sentences.zh: 至秦並天下，兼收六國車旗服御，窮極侈靡，有大駕、法駕以及鹵簿。

translations.literal: When Qin united the realm, it gathered together the carriages, banners, dress, and regalia of the six states, exhausting extravagance, with the grand escort, the statutory escort, and the guard of honor.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin united the empire, it absorbed the carriages, banners, dress, and regalia of the six states to an extreme of lavish display, establishing the grand escort, the statutory escort, and the imperial guard of honor.

sentences.zh: 漢承秦後，多因其舊。

translations.literal: Han succeeded Qin and largely followed its precedents.
translations.idiomatic: The Han followed Qin and for the most part retained its institutions.

sentences.zh: 由唐及宋，亦效秦法，以為盛典。

translations.literal: From Tang through Song, they also imitated Qin law and took it as a grand canonical model.
translations.idiomatic: From Tang through Song as well, courts imitated Qin practice and treated it as the grand ceremonial standard.

sentences.zh: 於文質適中之義，君子或得而議焉。

translations.literal: As for the meaning of suiting ornament to substance, gentlemen could sometimes discuss it.
translations.idiomatic: On the question of balancing refinement and plain substance, men of discernment might sometimes raise objections.

sentences.zh: 元初立國，庶事草創，冠服車輿，並從舊俗。

translations.literal: When the Yuan first established the state, all affairs were newly begun; caps, dress, carriages, and chariots all followed old custom.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yuan first founded the dynasty, every institution was still being improvised, and caps, dress, carriages, and chariots all followed earlier custom.

sentences.zh: 世祖混一天下，近取金、宋，遠法漢、唐。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor unified the realm, taking nearby from Jin and Song and modeling distantly on Han and Tang.
translations.idiomatic: After the Founding Emperor unified the realm, he drew on Jin and Song for recent models and looked back to Han and Tang for distant precedent.

sentences.zh: 至英宗親祀太廟，復置鹵簿。

translations.literal: By the time of Emperor Yingzong's personal sacrifice at the Grand Temple, the guard of honor was restored.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong personally sacrificed at the Grand Ancestral Temple, the imperial guard of honor was restored.

sentences.zh: 今考之當時，上而天子之冕服，皇太子冠服，天子之質孫，天子之五輅與腰輿、象轎，以及儀衛隊仗，下而百官祭服、朝服，與百官之質孫，以及於士庶人之服色，粲然其有章，秩然其有序。

translations.literal: Now examining that time, from above—the Son of Heaven's ceremonial dress, the crown prince's cap and dress, the Son of Heaven's zhisun, the Son of Heaven's five carriages with waist litters and elephant palanquins, and the ceremonial guards and weaponry—down to the hundred officials' sacrificial dress and court dress, the hundred officials' zhisun, and even the dress colors of gentlemen and commoners—brilliantly they had pattern, orderly they had sequence.
translations.idiomatic: Examining the institutions of that age, one finds above the Son of Heaven's ceremonial robes and caps, the crown prince's court dress, the emperor's zhisun regalia, the five state carriages together with waist litters and elephant palanquins, and the ceremonial guards and arms; and below, the sacrificial and court dress of officials, officials' zhisun regalia, and even the regulated colors worn by gentlemen and commoners—all brilliantly patterned and rigorously ordered.

sentences.zh: 大抵參酌古今，隨時損益，兼存國制，用備儀文。

translations.literal: In general they weighed ancient and modern, reducing and augmenting according to the times, preserving together national institutions to complete ritual forms.
translations.idiomatic: In general these regulations weighed past and present, adjusting them to the needs of the age while preserving native Yuan custom, thereby completing the full corpus of ritual protocol.

sentences.zh: 於是朝廷之盛，宗廟之美，百官之富，有以成一代之制作矣。

translations.literal: Thus the splendor of the court, the beauty of the ancestral temples, and the richness of the hundred officials had the means to complete the institutions of an age.
translations.idiomatic: In this way the splendor of the court, the dignity of the ancestral temples, and the full array of official regalia together constituted the ceremonial achievement of a dynasty.

sentences.zh: 作《輿服志》，而儀衛附見於後云。

translations.literal: The 《Treatise on Carriages and Clothes》 was composed, with Ceremonial Escort appended and seen afterward.
translations.idiomatic: The 《Treatise on Carriages and Clothes》 was therefore compiled, with Ceremonial Escort appended at the end.

sentences.zh: ○冕服

translations.literal: ○ Ceremonial Caps and Robes
translations.idiomatic: Ceremonial Caps and Robes

sentences.zh: 天子冕服：袞冕，制以漆紗，上覆曰綖，青表朱裏。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven's ceremonial dress: the ancestral cap and robes, made of lacquered gauze; the covering above is called the board, green outside and vermilion inside.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven's ceremonial dress: for the ancestral temple cap and robes, lacquered gauze was used; the upper covering is called the cap board, green on the outside and vermilion within.

sentences.zh: 綖之四周，匝以雲龍。

translations.literal: Around the four sides of the board, cloud-dragons encircled it.
translations.idiomatic: Around all four sides of the cap board, cloud-and-dragon motifs ran in a band.

sentences.zh: 冠之口圍，縈以珍珠。

translations.literal: The mouth of the cap was encircled with pearls.
translations.idiomatic: The rim of the cap was ringed with pearls.

sentences.zh: 綖之前後，旒各十二，以珍珠為之。

translations.literal: Before and behind the board, there were twelve pendants each, made of pearls.
translations.idiomatic: Before and behind the cap board hung twelve pendants each, all of pearls.

sentences.zh: 綖之左右，系黈纊二，系以玄紞，承以玉瑱，纊色黃，絡以珠。

translations.literal: To the left and right of the board were attached two yellow earplugs, fastened with black cords, supported by jade plugs; the plugs were yellow and netted with pearls.
translations.idiomatic: On either side of the board hung two yellow earplugs, secured with black cords and supported by jade stoppers; the plugs were yellow and strung with pearls.

sentences.zh: 冠之周圍，珠雲龍網結，通翠柳調珠。

translations.literal: Around the cap, pearl cloud-dragon nets were knotted, threaded through with kingfisher willow and strung pearls.
translations.idiomatic: Around the cap, knotted nets of pearl cloud-dragons were threaded with kingfisher willow ornaments and strung pearls.

sentences.zh: 綖上橫天河帶一，左右至地。

translations.literal: Across the board lay one Milky Way band, extending left and right to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: A Milky Way band crossed the cap board horizontally, its ends reaching to the ground on either side.

sentences.zh: 珠鈿窠網結，翠柳朱絲組二，屬諸笄，為纓絡，以翠柳調珠。

translations.literal: Pearl inlay nests were net-knotted; two kingfisher willow and vermilion silk tassels were attached to the hairpins as chin straps, strung with kingfisher willow and pearls.
translations.idiomatic: Pearl-inlaid net knots were worked in; two chin straps of kingfisher willow and vermilion silk were attached to the hairpins and strung with kingfisher willow and pearls.

sentences.zh: 簪以玉為之，橫貫於冠。

translations.literal: The hairpin was made of jade and passed horizontally through the cap.
translations.idiomatic: The hairpin was of jade and passed horizontally through the cap.

sentences.zh: 袞龍服，制以青羅，飾以生色銷金帝星一、日一、月一、升龍四、復身龍四、山三十八、火四十八、華蟲四十八、虎蜼四十八。

translations.literal: The dragon robe was made of green gauze, decorated with living-color cut-gold: one Imperial Star, one sun, one moon, four ascending dragons, four full-body dragons, thirty-eight mountains, forty-eight fires, forty-eight splendid creatures, and forty-eight tiger-moths.
translations.idiomatic: The dragon robe was made of green gauze and decorated in polychrome cut gold with one Imperial Star, one sun, one moon, four ascending dragons, four full-body dragons, thirty-eight mountains, forty-eight fires, forty-eight splendid creatures, and forty-eight tiger-moths.

sentences.zh: 裳，制以緋羅，其狀如裙，飾以文繡，凡一十六行，每行藻二、粉米一、黼二、黻二。

translations.literal: The skirt was made of scarlet gauze, shaped like a pleated skirt, decorated with figured embroidery: sixteen rows in all, each row with two water-weeds, one grain powder, two axes, and two opposed triangles.
translations.idiomatic: The skirt was of scarlet gauze in pleated form, embroidered with sixteen rows in all, each row bearing two water-weeds, one grain emblem, two axes, and two opposed triangles.

sentences.zh: 中單，制以白紗，絳緣，黃勒帛副之。

translations.literal: The inner robe was made of white gauze with crimson border; a yellow girdle cloth was added.
translations.idiomatic: The inner robe was of white gauze with a crimson border, supplemented by a yellow girdle cloth.

sentences.zh: 蔽膝，制以緋羅，有褾。

translations.literal: The knee cover was made of scarlet gauze and had a border strip.
translations.idiomatic: The knee cover was made of scarlet gauze with a hem border.

sentences.zh: 緋絹為裏，其形如襜，袍上着之，繡複身龍。

translations.literal: Scarlet silk formed the lining; its shape was like a apron, worn over the robe, embroidered with full-body dragons.
translations.idiomatic: Its lining was scarlet silk; shaped like an apron and worn over the robe, it was embroidered with full-body dragons.

sentences.zh: 玉佩，珩一、琚一、瑀一、沖牙一、璜二。

translations.literal: The jade pendant set: one top plaque, one middle plaque, one lower plaque, one angle tooth, and two arc plaques.
translations.idiomatic: The jade pendant set comprised one top plaque, one middle plaque, one lower plaque, one angle tooth, and two arc plaques.

sentences.zh: 沖牙以系璜，珩下有銀獸面，塗以黃金，雙璜夾之。

translations.literal: The angle tooth fastened the arc plaques; below the top plaque was a silver beast mask gilded with gold, with twin arc plaques flanking it.
translations.idiomatic: The angle tooth linked the arc plaques; beneath the top plaque was a silver beast mask gilded in gold, flanked by twin arc plaques.

sentences.zh: 次又有衡，下有沖牙。

translations.literal: Next there was again a crossbar, with an angle tooth below.
translations.idiomatic: Below that was another crossbar, with an angle tooth beneath it.

sentences.zh: 傍別施雙的以鳴，用玉。

translations.literal: At the sides were separately attached twin sounding stones to ring, made of jade.
translations.idiomatic: At the sides were separately hung twin sounding plaques of jade to chime.

sentences.zh: 大帶，制以緋白二色羅，合縫為之。

translations.literal: The great belt was made of scarlet and white two-colored gauze, sewn together.
translations.idiomatic: The great belt was made of scarlet and white gauze sewn together.

sentences.zh: 玉環綬，制以納石失。

translations.literal: The jade-ring sash was made of nasiji.
translations.idiomatic: The jade-ring sash was made of nasiji brocade.

translations.literal: (It is gold brocade.)
translations.idiomatic: The gloss identifies nasiji as gold brocade.〉

sentences.zh: 上有三小玉環，下有青絲織網。

translations.literal: Above were three small jade rings; below was a green silk woven net.
translations.idiomatic: It bore three small jade rings above and a green silk woven net below.

sentences.zh: 紅羅靴，制以紅羅為之，高靿。

translations.literal: Red gauze boots were made of red gauze with high shafts.
translations.idiomatic: Red gauze boots were made of red gauze with high shafts.

sentences.zh: 履，制以納石失，有雙耳二，帶鉤，飾以珠。

translations.literal: Slippers were made of nasiji, with two paired flaps, belt hooks, and pearl ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Slippers were made of nasiji brocade, with two side flaps, belt hooks, and pearl ornamentation.

sentences.zh: 襪，制以紅綾。

translations.literal: Socks were made of red damask.
translations.idiomatic: Socks were made of red damask.

sentences.zh: 右按《太常集禮》，至元十二年十一月，博士議擬：冕天版長一尺六寸，廣八寸，前高八寸五分，後高九寸五分，身圍一尺八寸三分，並納言，用青羅為表，紅羅為裏，周回緣以黃金。

translations.literal: According to the 《Collected Rites of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices》, in the eleventh month of the twelfth year of Zhiyuan, erudites deliberated and proposed: the cap's heaven board was one foot six inches long, eight inches wide, eight inches five fen high in front, nine inches five fen high behind, one foot eight inches three fen in girth including the front flap; green gauze was used for the outside, red gauze for the lining, and gold bordered it all around.
translations.idiomatic: According to the 《Collected Rites of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices》, in the eleventh month of the twelfth year of Zhiyuan, erudites proposed the following: the cap's heaven board should measure one foot six inches long and eight inches wide, eight and a half inches high in front and nine and a half inches behind, with a total girth of one foot eight and a third inches including the front flap; green gauze was to form the outer layer and red gauze the lining, with gold bordering the entire circumference.

sentences.zh: 天版下四面，珠網結子，花素墜子，前後共二十有四旒，以珍珠為之。

translations.literal: On the four sides beneath the heaven board were pearl net knots, plain floral pendants; before and behind there were twenty-four pendants in all, made of pearls.
translations.idiomatic: On all four sides beneath the heaven board were pearl net knots and plain floral pendants; twenty-four pendants in all hung before and behind, all of pearls.

sentences.zh: 青碧線織天河帶，兩頭各有珍珠金翠旒三節，玉滴子節花全。

translations.literal: A Milky Way band was woven of green jade-green thread; at each end were three sections of pearl, gold, and kingfisher pendants, with jade drops and full floral nodes.
translations.idiomatic: A Milky Way band was woven in green and blue thread; at each end were three sections of pearl, gold, and kingfisher pendants, complete with jade drops and floral nodes.

sentences.zh: 紅線組帶二，上有珍珠金翠旒，玉滴子，下有金鐸二。

translations.literal: Two red cord tassel bands had pearl, gold, and kingfisher pendants above and jade drops; below were two gold bells.
translations.idiomatic: Two red cord tassel bands bore pearl, gold, and kingfisher pendants and jade drops above, with two gold bells below.

sentences.zh: 梅紅繡款幔帶一，黈纊二，珍珠垂系，上用金萼子二。

translations.literal: One plum-red embroidered patterned curtain band, two yellow earplugs, pearl pendants hanging, with two gold calyx mounts used above.
translations.idiomatic: There was one plum-red embroidered patterned curtain band, two yellow earplugs with hanging pearl pendants, and two gold calyx mounts above.

sentences.zh: 簪窠款幔組帶鈿窠各二，內組帶窠四，並鏤玉為之。

translations.literal: Hairpin nests, patterned curtain bands, and inlay nests—two each; inner band nests, four—all carved in jade.
translations.idiomatic: Two each of hairpin nests, patterned curtain bands, and inlay nests, plus four inner band nests—all carved in jade.

sentences.zh: 玉簪一，頂面鏤雲龍。

translations.literal: One jade hairpin, its top surface carved with cloud-dragons.
translations.idiomatic: One jade hairpin, its crown carved with cloud-dragons.

sentences.zh: 袞衣，用青羅夾制，五采間金，繪日、月、星辰、山、龍、華蟲、宗彜。

translations.literal: The dragon robe used green gauze in layered make, five colors interwoven with gold, painted with sun, moon, stars, mountains, dragons, splendid creatures, and ritual vessels.
translations.idiomatic: The dragon robe was of layered green gauze, the five colors interwoven with gold and painted with the sun, moon, stars, mountains, dragons, splendid creatures, and ritual vessels.

sentences.zh: 正面日一，月一，升龍四，山十二，上下襟華蟲、火各六對，虎蜼各

translations.literal: On the front: one sun, one moon, four ascending dragons, twelve mountains; on the upper and lower flaps, splendid creatures and fire, six pairs each; tiger-moths each
translations.idiomatic: On the front were one sun, one moon, four ascending dragons, and twelve mountains; on the upper and lower flaps, six pairs each of splendid creatures and of fire; tiger-moths, each

translations.literal: (lacuna)
translations.idiomatic: (text missing)

sentences.zh: 對，背星一，升龍四，山十二，華蟲、火各十二對，虎蜼各六對。

translations.literal: pair; on the back one star, four ascending dragons, twelve mountains, splendid creatures and fire twelve pairs each, tiger-moths six pairs each.
translations.idiomatic: pair; on the back were one star, four ascending dragons, twelve mountains, twelve pairs each of splendid creatures and of fire, and six pairs of tiger-moths.

sentences.zh: 中單，用白羅單制，羅領褾襈。

translations.literal: The inner robe used white gauze in single layer, with gauze collar and bordered cuffs.
translations.idiomatic: The inner robe was of single-layer white gauze with a gauze collar and bordered cuffs.

sentences.zh: 裳一，帶褾襈全，紅羅八幅夾造。

translations.literal: One skirt, with full border and cuffs, made of eight panels of layered red gauze.
translations.idiomatic: One skirt, fully bordered and cuffed, made of eight panels of layered red gauze.

sentences.zh: 上繡藻、粉米、黼、黻，藻三十二，粉米十六，黼三十二，黻三十二。

translations.literal: Embroidered above were water-weeds, grain powder, axes, and opposed triangles: thirty-two water-weeds, sixteen grain powder, thirty-two axes, thirty-two opposed triangles.
translations.idiomatic: It was embroidered with water-weeds, grain emblems, axes, and opposed triangles: thirty-two water-weeds, sixteen grain emblems, thirty-two axes, and thirty-two opposed triangles.

sentences.zh: 蔽膝一，帶褾襈，紅羅夾造八幅，上繡升龍二。

translations.literal: One knee cover, with border and cuffs, eight panels of layered red gauze, embroidered above with two ascending dragons.
translations.idiomatic: One knee cover, bordered and cuffed, of eight panels of layered red gauze, embroidered above with two ascending dragons.

sentences.zh: 綬一幅，六采織造，紅羅托裏。

translations.literal: One sash panel, woven in six colors, with red gauze backing.
translations.idiomatic: One sash panel, woven in six colors with a red gauze backing.

sentences.zh: 小綬三，色同大綬，銷金黃羅綬頭全，上間施二玉環，並碾雲龍。

translations.literal: Three small sashes, the same colors as the great sash, with full cut-gold yellow gauze sash heads; between them were set two jade rings, both ground with cloud-dragons.
translations.idiomatic: Three small sashes matching the great sash in color, with full cut-gold yellow gauze sash heads; two jade rings were set between them, both ground with cloud-dragons.

sentences.zh: 緋白大帶一，銷金黃帶頭，鈿窠二十有四。

translations.literal: One scarlet-and-white great belt, with cut-gold yellow belt head and twenty-four inlay nests.
translations.idiomatic: One scarlet-and-white great belt with a cut-gold yellow belt head and twenty-four inlay nests.

sentences.zh: 紅羅勒帛一，青羅抹帶一。

translations.literal: One red gauze girdle cloth, one green gauze sash band.
translations.idiomatic: One red gauze girdle cloth and one green gauze sash band.

sentences.zh: 佩二，玉上、中、下璜各一，半月各二，並碾玉為雲龍文。

translations.literal: Two pendant sets: one each of upper, middle, and lower arc plaques, and two half-moons each—all jade ground with cloud-dragon pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Two pendant sets, each with one upper, middle, and lower arc plaque and two half-moon pieces—all jade ground with cloud-dragon designs.

sentences.zh: 玉滴子各二，並珍珠穿造。

translations.literal: Two jade drops each, all strung with pearls.
translations.idiomatic: Two jade drops each, all strung together with pearls.

sentences.zh: 金篦鉤，獸面，水葉環釘全。

translations.literal: Gold comb-hooks, beast faces, and full water-leaf ring nails.
translations.idiomatic: Gold comb-hooks with beast faces and complete water-leaf ring nails.

sentences.zh: 涼帶一，紅羅裏，鏤金為之；

translations.literal: One cool belt, red gauze lined, made of pierced gold;
translations.idiomatic: One cool belt, red gauze lined and made of pierced gold;

sentences.zh: 上為玉鵝七，撻尾束各一，金攀龍口，玳瑁襯釘。

translations.literal: above were seven jade geese, one lash-tail clasp each, gold dragon-clasp mouths, and tortoiseshell backing nails.
translations.idiomatic: bearing seven jade geese above, one lash-tail clasp each, gold dragon-clasp mouths, and tortoiseshell backing nails.

sentences.zh: 舄一，重底，紅羅面，白綾托裏，如意頭，銷金黃羅緣口，玉鼻，純飾以珍珠。

translations.literal: One pair of shoes, double-soled, red gauze upper, white damask backing, ruyi toe, cut-gold yellow gauze border at the mouth, jade nose, ornamented purely with pearls.
translations.idiomatic: One pair of shoes with double soles, red gauze uppers and white damask lining, ruyi-shaped toes, cut-gold yellow gauze borders, jade nose pieces, and ornamentation entirely of pearls.

sentences.zh: 金緋羅錦襪一兩。
