sentences.zh: 〈（綴小珠於金錦。）〉

translations.literal: (Small pearls set on gold brocade.)
translations.idiomatic: The gloss notes small pearls set on gold brocade.〉

sentences.zh: 則冠珠子卷雲冠。

translations.literal: Then one wore a pearl scrolling-cloud crown.
translations.idiomatic: he wore a pearl scrolling-cloud crown.

sentences.zh: 服納石失，則帽亦如之。

translations.literal: Wearing nasiji, the cap was likewise.
translations.idiomatic: When he wore nasiji, he wore the matching cap as well.

sentences.zh: 服大紅珠寶裏紅毛子答納，則冠珠緣邊鈸笠。

translations.literal: Wearing great-red pearl baoli with red fur dana, one wore a pearl-edged cymbal hat.
translations.idiomatic: When he wore great-red pearl baoli with red fur dana, he wore a pearl-edged cymbal hat.

sentences.zh: 服白毛子金絲寶裏，則冠白藤寶貝帽。

translations.literal: Wearing white fur with gold-thread baoli, one wore a white-rattan shell hat.
translations.idiomatic: When he wore white fur with gold-thread baoli, he wore a white-rattan shell hat.

sentences.zh: 服駝褐毛子，則帽亦如之。

translations.literal: Wearing camel-brown fur, the cap was likewise.
translations.idiomatic: When he wore camel-brown fur, he wore the matching cap as well.

sentences.zh: 服大紅、綠、藍、銀褐、棗褐、金繡龍五色羅，則冠金鳳頂笠，各隨其服之色。

translations.literal: Wearing great-red, green, blue, silver-brown, jujube-brown, and gold-embroidered dragon five-color gauze, one wore a golden-phoenix-peaked hat, each following the color of its garment.
translations.idiomatic: When he wore great-red, green, blue, silver-brown, jujube-brown, or gold-embroidered dragon five-color gauze, he wore a golden-phoenix-peaked hat in the corresponding color.

sentences.zh: 服金龍青羅，則冠金鳳頂漆紗冠。

translations.literal: Wearing gold-dragon green gauze, one wore a golden-phoenix-peaked lacquered-gauze crown.
translations.idiomatic: When he wore gold-dragon green gauze, he wore a golden-phoenix-peaked lacquered-gauze crown.

sentences.zh: 服珠子褐七寶珠龍褡子，則冠黃牙忽寶貝珠子帶後檐帽。

translations.literal: Wearing pearl-brown seven-jewel pearl-dragon dazi, one wore a yellow yahu shell-and-pearl rear-brim hat.
translations.idiomatic: When he wore pearl-brown seven-jewel pearl-dragon dazi, he wore a yellow yahu shell-and-pearl rear-brim hat.

sentences.zh: 服青速夫金絲襕子，

translations.literal: Wearing blue suf gold-thread lam robes,
translations.idiomatic: When he wore blue suf lam robes with gold thread,

sentences.zh: 〈（速夫，回回毛布之精者也。）〉

translations.literal: (Suf—the finest Hui wool cloth.)
translations.idiomatic: The gloss explains that suf is the finest Hui wool cloth.〉

sentences.zh: 則冠七寶漆紗帶後檐帽。

translations.literal: Then one wore a seven-jewel lacquered-gauze rear-brim hat.
translations.idiomatic: he wore a seven-jewel lacquered-gauze rear-brim hat.

sentences.zh: 百官質孫，冬之服凡九等，大紅納石失一，大紅怯綿裏一，大紅冠素一，桃紅、藍、綠官素各一，紫、黃、鴉青各一。

translations.literal: Hundred officials' zhisun: winter dress had nine grades in all—one great-red nasiji, one great-red qiemian lining, one great-red plain cap cloth, one each of peach-red, blue, and green official plain cloth, and one each of purple, yellow, and crow-blue.
translations.idiomatic: Officials' zhisun winter dress comprised nine grades: one each of great-red nasiji, great-red qiemian lining, and great-red plain cap cloth; one each of peach-red, blue, and green official plain cloth; and one each of purple, yellow, and crow-blue.

sentences.zh: 夏之服凡十有四等，素納石失一，聚線寶裏納石失一，棗褐渾金間絲蛤珠一，大紅官素帶寶裏一，大紅明珠答子一，桃紅、藍、綠、銀褐各一，高麗鴉青雲袖羅一，駝褐、茜紅、白毛子各一，鴉青官素帶寶裏一。

translations.literal: Summer dress had fourteen grades in all—one plain nasiji, one clustered-thread baoli nasiji, one jujube-brown all-gold interwoven silk clam-pearl, one great-red official plain baoli, one great-red bright-pearl dana, one each of peach-red, blue, green, and silver-brown, one Goryeo crow-blue cloud-sleeve gauze, one each of camel-brown, madder-red, and white fur, and one crow-blue official plain baoli.
translations.idiomatic: Officials' zhisun summer dress comprised fourteen grades: one plain nasiji, one clustered-thread baoli nasiji, one jujube-brown all-gold interwoven silk with clam pearls, one great-red official plain baoli, one great-red bright-pearl dana, one each of peach-red, blue, green, and silver-brown, one Goryeo crow-blue cloud-sleeve gauze, one each of camel-brown, madder-red, and white fur, and one crow-blue official plain baoli.

sentences.zh: 百官公服：

translations.literal: Hundred officials' court robes:
translations.idiomatic: Court robes of the hundred officials:

sentences.zh: 公服，制以羅，大袖，盤領，俱右衽。

translations.literal: Court robes were made of gauze, with large sleeves, round collars, all right-lapped.
translations.idiomatic: Court robes were made of gauze with large sleeves and round collars, all fastened on the right.

sentences.zh: 一品紫，大獨科花，徑五寸。

translations.literal: First rank: purple, large solitary-branch flowers, five inches in diameter.
translations.idiomatic: First rank wore purple with large solitary-branch flowers five inches across.

sentences.zh: 二品小獨科花，徑三寸。

translations.literal: Second rank: small solitary-branch flowers, three inches in diameter.
translations.idiomatic: Second rank wore small solitary-branch flowers three inches across.

sentences.zh: 三品散答花，徑二寸，無枝葉。

translations.literal: Third rank: scattered da flowers, two inches in diameter, without branches or leaves.
translations.idiomatic: Third rank wore scattered da flowers two inches across, without branches or leaves.

sentences.zh: 四品、五品小雜花，徑一寸五分。

translations.literal: Fourth and fifth ranks: small mixed flowers, one and a half inches in diameter.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth and fifth ranks wore small mixed flowers one and a half inches across.

sentences.zh: 六品、七品緋羅小雜花，徑一寸。

translations.literal: Sixth and seventh ranks: scarlet gauze small mixed flowers, one inch in diameter.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth and seventh ranks wore scarlet gauze with small mixed flowers one inch across.

sentences.zh: 八品、九品綠羅，無文。

translations.literal: Eighth and ninth ranks: green gauze, without pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth and ninth ranks wore plain green gauze without ornament.

sentences.zh: 幞頭，漆紗為之，展其角。

translations.literal: Headcloths were made of lacquered gauze, with their corners spread.
translations.idiomatic: Headcloths were made of lacquered gauze with spread corners.

sentences.zh: 笏，制以牙，上圓下方。

translations.literal: Tablets were made of ivory, round above and square below.
translations.idiomatic: Tablets were made of ivory, rounded at the top and square at the bottom.

sentences.zh: 或以銀杏木為之。

translations.literal: Or they were made of ginkgo wood.
translations.idiomatic: Ginkgo wood might be used instead.

sentences.zh: 偏帶，正從一品以玉，或花，或素。

translations.literal: Side belts: regular and concurrent first rank used jade, either patterned or plain.
translations.idiomatic: For side belts, regular and concurrent first rank used jade plaques, either patterned or plain.

sentences.zh: 二品以花犀。

translations.literal: Second rank used patterned rhinoceros horn.
translations.idiomatic: Second rank wore side belts with patterned rhinoceros horn plaques.

sentences.zh: 三品、四品以黃金為荔枝。

translations.literal: Third and fourth ranks used gold cast as lychee fruit.
translations.idiomatic: Third and fourth ranks used gold plaques cast in the shape of lychee fruit.

sentences.zh: 五品以下以烏犀。

translations.literal: Fifth rank and below used black rhinoceros horn.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of fifth rank and below wore black rhinoceros horn plaques.

sentences.zh: 並八胯，鞓用朱革。

translations.literal: All had eight plaques; the belt cord used vermilion leather.
translations.idiomatic: All bore eight plaques, and the belt cord was made of vermilion leather.

sentences.zh: 靴，以皂皮為之。

translations.literal: Boots were made of black leather.
translations.idiomatic: Official boots were fashioned from black leather.

sentences.zh: 交角幞頭，其制，巾後交折其角。

translations.literal: Crossed-corner headcloths—their form folded the corners crossed behind the headcloth.
translations.idiomatic: Crossed-corner headcloths folded their corners crossed at the back.

sentences.zh: 鳳翅幞頭，制如唐巾，兩角上曲，而作雲頭，兩旁覆以兩金鳳翅。

translations.literal: Phoenix-wing headcloths were made like Tang headcloths, with both corners curving upward into cloud heads, and both sides covered by two golden phoenix wings.
translations.idiomatic: Phoenix-wing headcloths followed the Tang headcloth form, with upturned corners shaped as cloud heads and golden phoenix wings covering both sides.

sentences.zh: 學士帽，制如唐巾，兩角如匙頭下垂。

translations.literal: Scholar caps were made like Tang headcloths, with both corners like spoon heads hanging down.
translations.idiomatic: Scholar caps followed the Tang headcloth form, with both corners hanging down like spoon heads.

sentences.zh: 唐巾，制如幞頭，而撱其角，兩角上曲作雲頭。

translations.literal: Tang headcloths were made like headcloths, but with their corners folded up, both corners curving upward into cloud heads.
translations.idiomatic: Tang headcloths resembled standard headcloths, but with folded corners curving upward into cloud heads.

sentences.zh: 控鶴幞頭，制如交角，金縷其額。

translations.literal: Crane-keeping headcloths were made like crossed-corner headcloths, with the forehead gold filigreed.
translations.idiomatic: Crane-keeping headcloths followed the crossed-corner form, with a gold-filigreed forehead band.

sentences.zh: 花角幞頭，制如控鶴幞頭，兩角及額上，簇象生雜花。

translations.literal: Flower-corner headcloths were made like crane-keeping headcloths; on both corners and the forehead clustered lifelike mixed flowers.
translations.idiomatic: Flower-corner headcloths followed the crane-keeping form, with lifelike mixed flowers clustered on the corners and forehead.

sentences.zh: 錦帽，制以漆紗，後幅兩旁，前拱而高，中下，後畫連錢錦，前額作聚文。

translations.literal: Brocade caps were made of lacquered gauze, with rear panels on both sides, the front arched and high then descending; the rear was painted with linked-coin brocade, and the forehead bore clustered pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Brocade caps were made of lacquered gauze with side rear panels, a high arched front that sloped downward, linked-coin brocade painted at the rear, and clustered ornament on the forehead.

sentences.zh: 平巾幘，黑漆革為之，形如進賢冠之籠巾，或以青，或以白。

translations.literal: Level kerchiefs were made of black lacquered leather, shaped like the cage kerchief of the Advancement cap, either green or white.
translations.idiomatic: Level kerchiefs were made of black lacquered leather in the shape of the Advancement cap's cage kerchief, in either green or white.

sentences.zh: 武弁，制以皮，加漆。

translations.literal: Military caps were made of leather and lacquered.
translations.idiomatic: Military caps were made of lacquered leather.

sentences.zh: 甲騎冠，制以皮，加黑漆，雌黃為緣。

translations.literal: Armored cavalry caps were made of leather, lacquered black, with orpiment as border.
translations.idiomatic: Armored cavalry caps were made of black-lacquered leather with orpiment borders.

sentences.zh: 抹額，制以緋羅，繡寶花。

translations.literal: Forehead bands were made of scarlet gauze, embroidered with treasure flowers.
translations.idiomatic: Forehead bands were made of scarlet gauze embroidered with treasure flowers.

sentences.zh: 巾，制以絁，五色，畫寶相花。

translations.literal: Kerchiefs were made of silk tabby, in five colors, painted with udumbara flowers.
translations.idiomatic: Kerchiefs were made of five-colored silk tabby painted with udumbara flowers.

sentences.zh: 兜鍪，制以皮，金塗五色，各隨其甲。

translations.literal: Helmets were made of leather, gilded in five colors, each following its armor.
translations.idiomatic: Helmets were made of leather gilded in five colors to match the corresponding armor.

sentences.zh: 襯甲，制如雲肩，青錦質，緣以白錦，衷以氈，裏以白絹。

translations.literal: Lining armor was made like cloud shoulders: green brocade body, bordered with white brocade, padded with felt, lined with white silk.
translations.idiomatic: Lining armor followed the cloud-shoulder form, with a green brocade body bordered in white brocade, felt padding, and a white silk lining.

sentences.zh: 雲肩，制如四垂雲，青緣，黃羅五色，嵌金為之。

translations.literal: Cloud shoulders were made like four hanging clouds, with green borders, yellow gauze in five colors, inlaid with gold.
translations.idiomatic: Cloud shoulders were shaped like four hanging clouds, with green borders and five-colored yellow gauze inlaid with gold.

sentences.zh: 裲襠，制如衫。

translations.literal: Bingdang vests were made like shirts.
translations.idiomatic: Bingdang vests were cut like shirts.

sentences.zh: 襯袍，制用緋錦，武士所以裼裲襠。

translations.literal: Lining robes were made of scarlet brocade; what warriors used when wearing the bingdang vest.
translations.idiomatic: Lining robes were made of scarlet brocade and were what warriors wore beneath the bingdang vest.

sentences.zh: 士卒袍，制以絹絁，繪寶相花。

translations.literal: Soldiers' robes were made of silk tabby, painted with udumbara flowers.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers' robes were made of silk tabby painted with udumbara flowers.

sentences.zh: 窄袖袍，制以羅或絁。

translations.literal: Narrow-sleeved robes were made of gauze or tabby.
translations.idiomatic: Narrow-sleeved robes were made of gauze or silk tabby.

sentences.zh: 辮線襖，制如窄袖衫，腰作辮線細折。

translations.literal: Plaited-line jackets were made like narrow-sleeved shirts, with plaited-line fine folds at the waist.
translations.idiomatic: Plaited-line jackets followed the narrow-sleeved shirt form, with fine plaited folds at the waist.

sentences.zh: 控鶴襖，制以青緋二色錦，圓答寶相花。

translations.literal: Crane-keeping jackets were made of green and scarlet two-color brocade, with round da-flower udumbara blossoms.
translations.idiomatic: Crane-keeping jackets were made of green and scarlet brocade with round da-flower udumbara blossoms.

sentences.zh: 窄袖襖，長行輿士所服，紺緅色。

translations.literal: Narrow-sleeved jackets were worn by long-procession litter bearers, in dark purple.
translations.idiomatic: Narrow-sleeved jackets in dark purple were worn by long-procession litter bearers.

sentences.zh: 樂工襖，制以緋錦，明珠琵琶窄袖，辮線細折。

translations.literal: Musicians' jackets were made of scarlet brocade, with bright-pearl pipa narrow sleeves and plaited-line fine folds.
translations.idiomatic: Musicians' jackets were made of scarlet brocade with bright-pearl pipa narrow sleeves and fine plaited folds.

sentences.zh: 甲，覆膊、掩心、扞背、扞股，制以皮，或為虎文、獅子文，或施金鎧銷子文。

translations.literal: Armor—arm covers, chest guards, back guards, and thigh guards—was made of leather, either with tiger or lion pattern, or bearing gilded armor ring-mail pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Armor comprised arm covers, chest guards, back guards, and thigh guards made of leather, either patterned with tigers or lions or bearing gilded ring-mail ornament.

sentences.zh: 臂鞲，制以錦，綠絹為裏，有雙帶。

translations.literal: Arm guards were made of brocade, with green silk lining and double straps.
translations.idiomatic: Arm guards were made of brocade lined with green silk and fitted with double straps.

sentences.zh: 錦螣蛇，束麻長一丈一尺，裹以紅錦。

translations.literal: Brocade teng snakes: bound hemp one zhang one chi long, wrapped in red brocade.
translations.idiomatic: Brocade teng snakes were hemp bindings one zhang one chi long, wrapped in red brocade.

sentences.zh: 束帶，紅鞓雙獺尾，黃金塗銅胯，余同腰帶而狹小。

translations.literal: Belt clasps: red belt cord with double otter tails, gilded bronze plaques; the rest like waist belts but narrower.
translations.idiomatic: Belt clasps had red belt cords with double otter tails and gilded bronze plaques, otherwise resembling waist belts but narrower.

sentences.zh: 絳環，制以銅，黃金塗之。

translations.literal: Crimson rings were made of bronze and gilded.
translations.idiomatic: Crimson rings were made of gilded bronze.

sentences.zh: 汗胯，制以青錦，緣以銀褐錦，或繡撲獸，間以雲氣。

translations.literal: Sweat plaques were made of green brocade, bordered with silver-brown brocade, sometimes embroidered with pouncing beasts, interspersed with cloud vapor.
translations.idiomatic: Sweat plaques were made of green brocade bordered in silver-brown brocade, sometimes embroidered with pouncing-beast motifs and interspersed with cloud patterns.

sentences.zh: 行縢，以絹為之。

translations.literal: Leg bindings were made of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Leg bindings were made of silk tabby.

sentences.zh: 鞋，制以麻。

translations.literal: Shoes were made of hemp.
translations.idiomatic: Shoes were made of hemp.

sentences.zh: 䩺鞋，制以皮為履，而長其靿，縛於行縢之內。

translations.literal: Daweng shoes were made with leather soles, with lengthened uppers, bound inside the leg bindings.
translations.idiomatic: Daweng shoes had leather soles and extended uppers that were secured inside the leg bindings.

sentences.zh: 雲頭靴，制以皮，幫嵌雲朵，頭作雲象，䩺束於脛。

translations.literal: Cloud-head boots were made of leather; the sides inlaid with cloud forms, the toe shaped like a cloud; daweng bindings tied on the shins.
translations.idiomatic: Cloud-head boots were made of leather with cloud motifs inlaid on the sides and cloud-shaped toes, the daweng bindings tied around the shins.

sentences.zh: 服色等第：仁宗延祐元年冬十有二月，定服色等第，詔曰：「比年以來，所在士民，靡麗相尚，尊卑混淆，僭禮費財，朕所不取。

translations.literal: Dress-color grades: In the twelfth month of winter in Yanyou year 1 of Emperor Renzong, dress-color grades were fixed; an edict said: "In recent years, gentlemen and commoners everywhere have vied in splendor, noble and base have been confused, ritual has been overstepped and wealth wasted—this I do not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Dress-color grades: In the twelfth month of winter in Yanyou 1 (1314), Emperor Renzong fixed the grades of dress and ornament. An edict declared: "In recent years gentlemen and commoners everywhere have competed in finery, blurring distinctions of rank, overstepping ritual propriety, and squandering wealth—conduct I will not tolerate.

sentences.zh: 貴賤有章，益明國制，儉奢中節，可阜民財。」

translations.literal: Noble and base should have clear distinction, further clarifying the national system; thrift and luxury kept to the mean can enrich the people's wealth."
translations.idiomatic: Distinctions between high and low should be clearly marked to clarify the national regulations; moderation in extravagance and restraint will help enrich the people's resources."

sentences.zh: 命中書省定立服色等第於後。

translations.literal: He ordered the Secretariat to fix and establish dress-color grades as follows.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the Secretariat to establish the dress-color grades set forth below.

sentences.zh: 一，蒙古人不在禁限，及見當怯薛諸色人等，亦不在禁限，惟不許服龍鳳文。

translations.literal: One: Mongols were not within the prohibitions, and current Keshig personnel of various categories were also not within the prohibitions, only not permitted to wear dragon-and-phoenix patterns.
translations.idiomatic: First, Mongols were exempt from these restrictions, as were active Keshig personnel of all categories; only dragon-and-phoenix designs remained forbidden to them.

sentences.zh: 〈（龍謂五爪二角者。）〉

translations.literal: (Dragon means five claws and two horns.)
translations.idiomatic: The gloss notes that "dragon" denotes the five-clawed, two-horned form.〉

sentences.zh: 一，職官除龍鳳文外，一品、二品服渾金花，三品服金答子，四品、五品服雲袖帶襕，六品、七品服六花，八品、九品服四花。

translations.literal: One: For officeholders, apart from dragon-and-phoenix patterns, ranks one and two wore whole-gold blossoms, rank three wore gold dazi, ranks four and five wore cloud-sleeve bordered-hem robes, ranks six and seven wore six-blossom patterns, ranks eight and nine wore four-blossom patterns.
translations.idiomatic: First, for officeholders, apart from dragon-and-phoenix designs: ranks one and two wore whole-gold blossom ornament; rank three wore gold dazi; ranks four and five wore cloud-sleeve bordered-hem robes; ranks six and seven wore six-blossom patterns; and ranks eight and nine wore four-blossom patterns.

sentences.zh: 〈（職事散官從一高。）〉

translations.literal: (For duty ranks and honorary ranks, follow whichever is higher.)
translations.idiomatic: The gloss notes that for substantive and honorary ranks, the higher of the two governs.〉

sentences.zh: 系腰，五品以下許用銀，並減鐵。

translations.literal: Waist-belt attachments: ranks five and below were permitted to use silver, and iron was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: For waist-belt attachments, ranks five and below might use silver, with iron fittings reduced accordingly.

sentences.zh: 一，命婦衣服，一品至三品服渾金，四品、五品服金褡子，六品以下惟服銷金，並金紗褡子。

translations.literal: One: For titled ladies' garments, ranks one through three wore whole gold, ranks four and five wore gold dazi vests, rank six and below wore only cut-gold ornament and gold-gauze dazi vests.
translations.idiomatic: First, for titled ladies' dress: ranks one through three wore whole-gold ornament; ranks four and five wore gold dazi vests; ranks six and below wore only cut-gold decoration and gold-gauze dazi vests.

sentences.zh: 首飾，一品至三品許用金珠寶玉，四品、五品用金玉珍珠，六品以下用金，惟耳環用珠玉。

translations.literal: Head ornaments: ranks one through three were permitted to use gold, pearls, gems, and jade; ranks four and five used gold, jade, and pearls; rank six and below used gold, only earrings using pearls and jade.
translations.idiomatic: For head ornaments: ranks one through three might use gold, pearls, gems, and jade; ranks four and five might use gold, jade, and pearls; ranks six and below might use gold alone, with pearls and jade permitted only for earrings.

sentences.zh: 〈（同籍不限親疏，期親雖別籍，並出嫁同。）〉

translations.literal: (Same household register without limit of close or distant kin; mourning-grade close kin even if on separate registers, and married daughters all the same.)
translations.idiomatic: The gloss notes that entitlement followed the same household register regardless of closeness of kinship; mourning-grade close relatives counted even if registered separately, as did married daughters.〉

sentences.zh: 一，器皿，

translations.literal: One: Vessels,
translations.idiomatic: First, for vessels,

sentences.zh: 〈（謂茶酒器。）〉

translations.literal: (Meaning tea and wine vessels.)
translations.idiomatic: The gloss notes that this refers to tea and wine vessels.〉

sentences.zh: 除钑造龍鳳文不得使用外，一品至三品許用金玉，四品、五品惟臺盞用金，六品以下臺盞用鍍金，余並用銀。

translations.literal: Apart from chased dragon-and-phoenix patterns not permitted for use, ranks one through three were permitted to use gold and jade; ranks four and five used gold only for stem cups; rank six and below used gold-plated stem cups; the rest all used silver.
translations.idiomatic: Except that chased dragon-and-phoenix designs were forbidden, ranks one through three might use gold and jade; ranks four and five might use gold only for stem cups; ranks six and below might use gold-plated stem cups; and all other vessels were to be of silver.

sentences.zh: 一，帳幕，除不得用赭黃龍鳳文外，一品至三品許用金花刺繡紗羅，四品、五品用刺繡紗羅，六品以下用素紗羅。

translations.literal: One: For tents and curtains, apart from not being permitted to use ochre-yellow dragon-and-phoenix patterns, ranks one through three were permitted to use gold-flower embroidered gauze and damask, ranks four and five used embroidered gauze and damask, rank six and below used plain gauze and damask.
translations.idiomatic: First, for tents and curtains: apart from the prohibition on ochre-yellow dragon-and-phoenix designs, ranks one through three might use gold-flower embroidered gauze and damask; ranks four and five might use embroidered gauze and damask; and ranks six and below might use plain gauze and damask.

sentences.zh: 一，車輿，除不得用龍鳳文外，一品至三品許用間金妝飾銀螭頭、繡帶，青幔，四品、五品用素獅頭、繡帶、青幔，六品至九品用素雲頭、素帶、青幔。

translations.literal: One: For carriages, apart from not being permitted to use dragon-and-phoenix patterns, ranks one through three were permitted to use interspersed gold-decorated silver chi-dragon heads and embroidered bands with green curtains, ranks four and five used plain lion heads, embroidered bands, and green curtains, ranks six through nine used plain cloud heads, plain bands, and green curtains.
translations.idiomatic: First, for carriages: apart from dragon-and-phoenix designs, ranks one through three might use silver chi-dragon heads with interspersed gold decoration, embroidered bands, and green curtains; ranks four and five might use plain lion heads, embroidered bands, and green curtains; and ranks six through nine might use plain cloud heads, plain bands, and green curtains.

sentences.zh: 一，鞍轡，一品許飾以金玉，二品、三品飾以金，四品、五品飾以銀，六品以下並飾以鍮石銅鐵。

translations.literal: One: For saddles and bridles, rank one was permitted ornament of gold and jade, ranks two and three ornament of gold, ranks four and five ornament of silver, rank six and below all ornament of brass alloy, bronze, and iron.
translations.idiomatic: First, for saddles and bridles: rank one might be ornamented with gold and jade; ranks two and three with gold; ranks four and five with silver; and ranks six and below with brass alloy, bronze, and iron.

sentences.zh: 一，內外有出身，考滿應入流，見役人員服用，與九品同。

translations.literal: One: Those inside and outside the service with examination credentials, upon completing tenure and qualifying to enter the regular ranks, currently serving personnel in dress and use were the same as rank nine.
translations.idiomatic: First, clerks inside and outside the regular bureaucracy who held examination credentials, had completed tenure, and were eligible to enter the regular ranks were to dress, while in active service, according to rank nine.

sentences.zh: 一，授各投下令旨、鈞旨，有印信，見任勾當人員，亦與九品同。

translations.literal: One: Those granted orders and rescripts from various agencies, bearing seals, currently serving acting personnel were also the same as rank nine.
translations.idiomatic: First, acting personnel currently serving under sealed orders and rescripts issued by various agencies were also to dress according to rank nine.

sentences.zh: 一，庶人除不得服赭黃，惟許服暗花纻絲紬綾羅毛毳，帽笠不許飾用金玉，靴不得裁制花樣。

translations.literal: One: Commoners, apart from not being permitted to wear ochre-yellow, were only permitted to wear dark-pattern ramie silk, figured silk, damask, gauze, and woolens; caps and hats were not permitted ornament of gold and jade; boots were not permitted cut in patterned designs.
translations.idiomatic: First, commoners were forbidden ochre-yellow but might wear dark-pattern ramie silk, figured silk, damask, gauze, and woolens; caps and hats might not be ornamented with gold or jade; and boots might not be cut in decorative patterns.

sentences.zh: 首飾許用翠花，並金釵錍各一事，惟耳環用金珠碧甸，余並用銀。

translations.literal: Head ornaments were permitted kingfisher flowers, and one each of gold hairpin and belt plaque; only earrings used gold, pearls, and green jade inlay; the rest all used silver.
translations.idiomatic: For head ornaments they might use kingfisher-feather flowers, one gold hairpin, and one gold belt plaque; earrings alone might use gold, pearls, and green jade inlay; all other ornaments were to be of silver.

sentences.zh: 酒器許用銀壺瓶臺盞盂鏇，余並禁止。

translations.literal: Wine vessels were permitted silver ewers, bottles, stem cups, bowls, and shallow dishes; the rest all forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: For wine vessels they might use silver ewers, bottles, stem cups, bowls, and shallow dishes; all others were forbidden.

sentences.zh: 帳幕用紗絹，不得赭黃，車輿黑油，齊頭平頂皂幔。

translations.literal: Tents and curtains used gauze and silk, not permitted ochre-yellow; carriages black lacquer, level-headed flat-topped black curtains.
translations.idiomatic: Tents and curtains were to be of gauze and silk, not ochre-yellow; carriages were to be black-lacquered with level-headed, flat-topped black curtains.

sentences.zh: 一，諸色目人，除行營帳外，其餘並與庶人同。

translations.literal: One: Persons of various semu categories, apart from campaign tents, the rest all the same as commoners.
translations.idiomatic: First, persons of the various semu categories were subject to the same rules as commoners, except for campaign tents.

sentences.zh: 一，諸職官致仕，與見任同。

translations.literal: One: All officeholders in retirement were the same as those currently serving.
translations.idiomatic: First, retired officeholders were to dress the same as incumbents.

sentences.zh: 解降者，依應得品級，不敘者，與庶人同。

translations.literal: Those dismissed and demoted followed the rank they should receive; those not restored were the same as commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Those dismissed and demoted dressed according to the rank to which they were entitled; those not restored to rank dressed as commoners.

sentences.zh: 一，父祖有官，既沒年深，非犯除名不敘之限，其命婦及子孫與見任同。

translations.literal: One: Where father or grandfather had held office, long since deceased, not within the limits of crimes requiring removal of name and non-restoration, their titled ladies and descendants were the same as those currently serving.
translations.idiomatic: First, where a father or grandfather had held office and had long since died, provided the family was not within the limits for crimes requiring expulsion and permanent disqualification, his titled lady and descendants dressed the same as incumbents.

sentences.zh: 一，諸樂藝人等服用，與庶人同。

translations.literal: One: All musicians and performers in dress and use were the same as commoners.
translations.idiomatic: First, musicians and performers were to dress the same as commoners.

sentences.zh: 凡承應妝扮之物，不拘上例。

translations.literal: All items for performance costume and makeup were not bound by the above examples.
translations.idiomatic: Costume and makeup items used in performance were not subject to the above rules.

sentences.zh: 一，皂隸公使人，惟許服紬絹。

translations.literal: One: Black-clad runners and government messengers were only permitted to wear figured silk tabby.
translations.idiomatic: First, runners and government messengers were permitted to wear only figured silk tabby.

sentences.zh: 一，娼家出入，止服皂褙子，不得乘坐車馬，余依舊例。

translations.literal: One: When courtesans went out, they wore only black beizi jackets, were not permitted to ride in carriages or on horses; the rest followed the old precedents.
translations.idiomatic: First, when courtesans went abroad they might wear only black beizi jackets and might not ride in carriages or on horses; other rules followed established precedent.

sentences.zh: 一，今後漢人、高麗、南人等投充怯薛者，並在禁限。

translations.literal: One: From now on Han people, Koreans, southern people, and others who enrolled as Keshig were all within the prohibitions.
translations.idiomatic: First, henceforth Han Chinese, Koreans, southerners, and others who had enrolled as Keshig were subject to these restrictions.

sentences.zh: 一，服色等第，上得兼下，下不得僭上。

translations.literal: One: For dress-color grades, those above might combine with those below; those below were not permitted to overstep those above.
translations.idiomatic: First, within the dress-color grades, higher ranks might adopt lower-grade items, but lower ranks might not usurp higher-grade privilege.

sentences.zh: 違者，職官解見任，期年後降一等敘，余人決五十七下。

translations.literal: Violators: officeholders were removed from current posts; after one full year demoted one grade in restoration, others sentenced to fifty-seven strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Violators among officeholders were to be removed from their posts and, after one year, restored at one rank lower; all others were to receive fifty-seven strokes of the rod.

sentences.zh: 違禁之物，付告捉人充賞。

translations.literal: Prohibited items were given to the informant and apprehender as reward.
translations.idiomatic: Contraband items were to be awarded to the informant who reported and seized them.

sentences.zh: 有司禁治不嚴，從監察御史、廉訪司究治。

translations.literal: If supervising offices did not prohibit and control strictly, the censorial investigators and surveillance commissions were to investigate and punish.
translations.idiomatic: If the responsible offices failed to enforce the ban strictly, censorial investigators and surveillance commissions were to investigate and punish them.

sentences.zh: 禦賜之物，不在禁限。

translations.literal: Items bestowed by the emperor were not within the prohibitions.
translations.idiomatic: Items bestowed by the emperor were exempt from these restrictions.

sentences.zh: ○輿輅

translations.literal: ○ Imperial Palanquins
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Palanquins

sentences.zh: 玉輅。

translations.literal: Jade palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: The jade palanquin.

sentences.zh: 青質，金裝，青綠藻井，栲栳輪蓋。

translations.literal: Green body, gold fittings, green-blue caisson ceiling, wicker-style wheel canopy.
translations.idiomatic: It had a green body with gold fittings, a green-blue caisson ceiling, and a wicker-style wheel canopy.

sentences.zh: 外施金裝雕木雲龍，內盤碾玉福海圓龍一，頂上匝以金塗鍮石耀葉八十一。

translations.literal: Externally applied gold-fitted carved wood cloud-dragons; internally set one ground-jade Fortune Sea round dragon; at the top encircled with eighty-one gilded brass-alloy radiant leaves.
translations.idiomatic: The exterior bore gold-fitted carved cloud-dragons in wood; within was set one round dragon of ground jade on a Fortune Sea panel; and around the apex were eighty-one gilded brass-alloy radiant leaves.

sentences.zh: 上圍九者二，中圍九者三，下圍九者四。

translations.literal: Two upper encircling nines, three middle encircling nines, four lower encircling nines.
translations.idiomatic: There were two upper rings of nine, three middle rings of nine, and four lower rings of nine.

sentences.zh: 頂輪衣三重，上二重青繡雲龍瑞草，下一重無文。

translations.literal: Canopy-wheel coverings in three layers; the upper two layers green-embroidered cloud-dragons and auspicious plants, the lower layer without pattern.
translations.idiomatic: The canopy-wheel coverings came in three layers: the upper two were embroidered in green with cloud-dragons and auspicious plants, and the lower layer was plain.

sentences.zh: 輪衣內黃屋一，黃素纻絲瀝水，下周垂朱絲結網，青纻絲繡小帶四十八，帶頭綴金塗小銅鈴，青纻絲繡絡帶二。

translations.literal: Within the wheel coverings one yellow canopy; plain yellow ramie-silk drip-water skirt; below the circumference hung a crimson-silk knotted net; forty-eight small green ramie-silk embroidered bands; band heads set with gilded small bronze bells; two green ramie-silk embroidered lacing bands.
translations.idiomatic: Within the wheel coverings was a yellow canopy with a plain yellow ramie-silk drip skirt; below hung a crimson-silk knotted net, forty-eight small green ramie-silk embroidered bands with gilded bronze bells at the ends, and two green ramie-silk embroidered lacing bands.

sentences.zh: 頂輪平素面夾用青纻絲。

translations.literal: The canopy wheel's flat plain surface interleaved with green ramie silk.
translations.idiomatic: The flat plain surface of the canopy wheel was interleaved with green ramie silk.

sentences.zh: 蓋四周垂流蘇八，飾以五色茸線結網五重，金塗銅鈸五，金塗木珠二十有五。

translations.literal: The canopy on four sides hung eight tassels; ornamented with five layers of five-colored plush-thread knotted net; five gilded bronze cymbals; twenty-five gilded wood beads.
translations.idiomatic: Eight tassels hung from the four sides of the canopy, which was ornamented with five layers of five-colored plush-thread knotted net, five gilded bronze cymbals, and twenty-five gilded wood beads.

sentences.zh: 又系玉雜佩八，珩璜沖瑀全，金塗

translations.literal: Also attached eight jade assorted pendants, complete with heng, huang, chong, and yu; gilded
translations.idiomatic: Also attached were eight jade pendant sets complete with heng, huang, chong, and yu ornaments, along with gilded

sentences.zh: 鍮石鉤掛十六，黃茸貫頂天心直下十字繩二，各長三丈。

translations.literal: brass-alloy hook hangers sixteen; two yellow-plush cords running straight down from the canopy apex through the cross ropes, each three zhang long.
translations.idiomatic: brass-alloy hook hangers numbering sixteen, and two yellow-plush cords running straight down from the canopy apex along the cross ropes, each three zhang long.

sentences.zh: 蓋下立朱漆柱四。

translations.literal: Below the canopy stood four vermilion-lacquer posts.
translations.idiomatic: Four vermilion-lacquer posts stood beneath the canopy.

sentences.zh: 柱下直平盤，虛櫃，中欞三十，下外桄二。

translations.literal: Below the posts a straight flat platform, hollow cabinet, thirty inner lattice bars, two outer lower rails.
translations.idiomatic: Below the posts was a straight flat platform and hollow cabinet with thirty inner lattice bars and two outer lower rails.

sentences.zh: 漆繪犀、象、鸚鵡、錦雉、孔雀，隔窠嵌裝花板。

translations.literal: Lacquer-painted rhinoceros, elephant, parrot, golden pheasant, and peacock, in bordered compartments with inlaid decorative panels.
translations.idiomatic: Rhinoceroses, elephants, parrots, golden pheasants, and peacocks were lacquer-painted in bordered compartments with inlaid decorative panels.

sentences.zh: 櫃周朱漆勾闌，雲拱地霞葉百七十有九，下垂牙護泥虛板，並朱漆畫瑞草。

translations.literal: Around the cabinet vermilion-lacquer balustrades, cloud-arch ground sunset-leaves one hundred seventy-nine; hanging down ivory guard mud hollow boards, all vermilion-lacquer painted auspicious plants.
translations.idiomatic: Around the cabinet ran vermilion-lacquer balustrades with one hundred seventy-nine cloud-arch and sunset-leaf ornaments; below hung ivory-edged guard panels, all painted in vermilion lacquer with auspicious plants.

sentences.zh: 勾闌上玉行龍十，碾玉蹲龍十，孔雀羽臺九，水精面火珠七，金圈焰銅照八。

translations.literal: On the balustrades ten jade walking dragons, ten ground-jade crouching dragons, nine peacock-feather platforms, seven crystal-faced fire pearls, eight gold-ringed flame bronze mirrors.
translations.idiomatic: On the balustrades were ten jade walking dragons, ten ground-jade crouching dragons, nine peacock-feather platforms, seven crystal-faced fire pearls, and eight gold-ringed flame bronze mirrors.

sentences.zh: 輿下周垂朱絲結網，飾以金塗鍮石鐸三百，彩畫鍮石梅萼嵌網眼中。

translations.literal: Around the palanquin below hung a crimson-silk knotted net, ornamented with three hundred gilded brass-alloy bells, polychrome-painted brass-alloy plum blossoms inlaid in the net eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Around the lower part of the palanquin hung a crimson-silk knotted net ornamented with three hundred gilded brass-alloy bells and polychrome-painted brass-alloy plum blossoms set into the mesh.

sentences.zh: 輿之長轅三，界轅勾心各三，上下龍頭六。

translations.literal: The palanquin had three long shafts, three boundary-shaft heart-hooks each, six dragon heads above and below.
translations.idiomatic: The palanquin had three long shafts, three boundary-shaft heart-hooks on each, and six dragon heads above and below.

sentences.zh: 前轅引手玉螭頭三，並系以蹲龍。

translations.literal: On the front shafts three jade chi-dragon hand-grips, each also tied with crouching dragons.
translations.idiomatic: On the front shafts were three jade chi-dragon hand-grips, each tied with a crouching dragon.

sentences.zh: 後轅方罨頭三，桄頭十六，絟以蹲龍三。

translations.literal: On the rear shafts three square yantou heads, sixteen shaft heads, bound with three crouching dragons.
translations.idiomatic: On the rear shafts were three square yantou heads and sixteen shaft heads, bound with three crouching dragons.

sentences.zh: 轅頭衡一，兩端玉龍頭二，上列金塗銅鳳十二，含以金塗銅鈴。

translations.literal: One shaft-head crossbar, two jade dragon heads at the ends, above arranged twelve gilded bronze phoenixes, holding gilded bronze bells in their beaks.
translations.idiomatic: There was one shaft-head crossbar with jade dragon heads at both ends; above it stood twelve gilded bronze phoenixes holding gilded bronze bells in their beaks.

sentences.zh: 輿之軸一，輪二。

translations.literal: The palanquin had one axle, two wheels.
translations.idiomatic: The palanquin had one axle and two wheels.

sentences.zh: 軸之挲羅二，明轄蹲龍絟，並青漆。

translations.literal: Two axle-end collars on the axle, bright hub crouching-dragon bindings, all green lacquer.
translations.idiomatic: The axle had two end collars and bright-hub crouching-dragon bindings, all in green lacquer.

sentences.zh: 輪之輻各二十四，轂首壓貼金塗銅轂葉八十一，金塗鍮石擎耳戀攀四。

translations.literal: Each wheel twenty-four spokes; hub cap overlaid with eighty-one gilded bronze hub leaves; four gilded brass-alloy bearing-ear love-binders.
translations.idiomatic: Each wheel had twenty-four spokes; the hub cap was overlaid with eighty-one gilded bronze hub leaves; and there were four gilded brass-alloy bearing-ear love-binders.

sentences.zh: 櫃之前，朱漆金裝雲龍輅牌一，牌字以玉裝綴。

translations.literal: Before the cabinet, one vermilion-lacquer gold-fitted cloud-dragon palanquin plaque; the plaque characters inlaid with jade.
translations.idiomatic: Before the cabinet hung one vermilion-lacquer, gold-fitted cloud-dragon palanquin plaque with jade-inlaid characters.

sentences.zh: 輅之箱，四壁雕鎪漆畫填心隔窠龜文華板。

translations.literal: The palanquin box: four walls carved, engraved, lacquer-painted, filled-center compartmented tortoise-pattern decorative panels.
translations.idiomatic: The palanquin box had four walls of carved, engraved, lacquer-painted panels with filled centers, compartmented tortoise patterns, and ornamental boards.

sentences.zh: 上層左畫青龍，右畫白虎，前畫朱雀，後畫玄武。

translations.literal: Upper layer: left painted azure dragon, right white tiger, front vermilion bird, rear dark warrior.
translations.idiomatic: On the upper level the left side bore the azure dragon, the right the white tiger, the front the vermilion bird, and the rear the dark warrior.

sentences.zh: 輅之前額，玉行龍二，奉一水精珠，後額如之。

translations.literal: On the palanquin front brow, two jade walking dragons, presenting one crystal pearl; the rear brow the same.
translations.idiomatic: On the front brow of the palanquin two jade walking dragons presented a crystal pearl; the rear brow was the same.

sentences.zh: 前兩柱青茸鈴索五，貼金鸞和大響銅鈴十，金塗鍮石雙魚五。

translations.literal: On the front two posts five green-plush bell cords, ten gold-appliqué luan-harmony great-sounding bronze bells, five gilded brass-alloy double fish.
translations.idiomatic: On the front two posts were five green-plush bell cords, ten gold-appliqué luan-harmony great-sounding bronze bells, and five gilded brass-alloy double-fish ornaments.

sentences.zh: 下朱漆軾櫃一，櫃上金香球、金香寶、金香合、銀灰盤各一，並黃絲綬帶。

translations.literal: Below one vermilion-lacquer dashboard cabinet; on the cabinet one each of gold incense ball, gold incense treasure, gold incense box, silver ash tray, all with yellow silk cord bands.
translations.idiomatic: Below was one vermilion-lacquer dashboard cabinet bearing one each of a gold incense ball, gold incense censer, gold incense box, and silver ash tray, all with yellow silk cord bands.

sentences.zh: 輅之後，朱漆後對一，金塗曲戌，黃纻絲銷金雲龍門簾一，緋纻絲繡雲龍帶二。

translations.literal: Behind the palanquin, one vermilion-lacquer rear screen, gilded curved rack, one yellow ramie-silk cut-gold cloud-dragon door curtain, two scarlet ramie-silk embroidered cloud-dragon bands.
translations.idiomatic: Behind the palanquin stood one vermilion-lacquer rear screen and a gilded curved rack, with one yellow ramie-silk cut-gold cloud-dragon door curtain and two scarlet ramie-silk embroidered cloud-dragon bands.

sentences.zh: 輅之中，金塗鍮石鉸碾玉龍椅一，靠背上金塗圈焰玉明珠一。

translations.literal: Within the palanquin, one gilded brass-alloy hinged ground-jade dragon chair; on the backrest one gilded ring-flame jade bright pearl.
translations.idiomatic: Within the palanquin was one gilded brass-alloy hinged ground-jade dragon chair with a gilded ring-flame jade bright pearl on the backrest.

sentences.zh: 右建太常旗，十有二斿，青羅繡日、月、五星、升龍。

translations.literal: On the right erected the Grand Constant flag, twelve tassel-streamers, green gauze embroidered with sun, moon, five stars, and ascending dragon.
translations.idiomatic: On the right was erected the Grand Constant flag with twelve streamers, of green gauze embroidered with the sun, moon, five stars, and an ascending dragon.

sentences.zh: 右建阘戟一，九斿，青羅繡雲龍。

translations.literal: On the right erected one tae halberd, nine streamers, green gauze embroidered cloud-dragon.
translations.idiomatic: On the right was also erected one tae halberd with nine streamers of green gauze embroidered with cloud-dragons.

sentences.zh: 中央黃羅繡青黑黼文兩旗，綢杠，並青羅，旗首金塗鍮石龍頭二，金塗銅鈴二，金塗鍮石鈸青纓緌十二重，金塗木珠流蘇十二重。

translations.literal: At the center two yellow gauze flags embroidered with green-black fu pattern, silk-cord poles, all green gauze; flag heads with two gilded brass-alloy dragon heads, two gilded bronze bells, twelve layers of gilded brass-alloy cymbal green tassels and cords, twelve layers of gilded wood-bead tassels.
translations.idiomatic: At the center were two yellow gauze flags embroidered with green-black fu patterns on silk-cord poles, all of green gauze; each flag head bore two gilded brass-alloy dragon heads and two gilded bronze bells, with twelve layers of gilded brass-alloy cymbals and green tassels and cords, and twelve layers of gilded wood-bead tassels.

sentences.zh: 龍椅上，方坐一，綠褥一，皆錦。

translations.literal: On the dragon chair, one square mat, one green cushion, all brocade.
translations.idiomatic: On the dragon chair were one square mat and one green cushion, both of brocade.

sentences.zh: 銷金黃羅夾帕一，方輿地褥二，勾闌內褥八，皆用雜錦綺。

translations.literal: One cut-gold yellow gauze sandwiched screen, two square palanquin floor mats, eight mats within the balustrade, all using mixed brocade and damask.
translations.idiomatic: There was one cut-gold yellow gauze sandwiched screen, two square palanquin floor mats, and eight mats within the balustrade, all of mixed brocade and damask.

sentences.zh: 青漆金塗鍮石鉸葉踏道一，小褥五重。

translations.literal: One green-lacquer gilded brass-alloy hinged-leaf step, five layers of small mats.
translations.idiomatic: There was one green-lacquer gilded brass-alloy hinged-leaf step and five layers of small mats.

sentences.zh: 青漆雕木塗金龍頭行馬一，小青漆梯一，青漆柄金塗長托叉二，短托叉二，金塗首青漆推竿一，青茸引輅索二，各長六丈餘，金塗銅環二，黃茸綏一。

translations.literal: One green-lacquer carved wood gold-coated dragon-head running horse, one small green-lacquer ladder, two green-lacquer-handled gilded long support forks, two short support forks, one gilded-head green-lacquer pushing pole, two green-plush palanquin-pulling ropes each more than six zhang long, two gilded bronze rings, one yellow-plush cord.
translations.idiomatic: Equipment included one green-lacquer carved wooden dragon-head running horse coated in gold, one small green-lacquer ladder, two long and two short gilded support forks with green-lacquer handles, one green-lacquer pushing pole with a gilded head, two green-plush palanquin-pulling ropes each more than six zhang long, two gilded bronze rings, and one yellow-plush cord.

sentences.zh: 輅馬、誕馬，並青色。

translations.literal: Palanquin horses and guide horses, all green.
translations.idiomatic: The palanquin horses and guide horses were all green.

sentences.zh: 鞍轡鞦勒纓拂靷，並青韋，金飾。

translations.literal: Saddles, bridles, cruppers, girths, tassels, whisk-feathers, cheek-pieces—all green leather, gold ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Saddles, bridles, cruppers, girths, tassels, whisk-feathers, and cheek-pieces were all of green leather with gold ornament.

sentences.zh: 誕馬青織金纻絲屜四副。

translations.literal: Guide horses: four sets green woven-gold ramie-silk shin guards.
translations.idiomatic: The guide horses had four sets of green woven-gold ramie-silk shin guards.

sentences.zh: 青羅銷金絹裏籠鞍六。

translations.literal: Six green gauze cut-gold silk-lined cage saddles.
translations.idiomatic: There were six green gauze cut-gold silk-lined cage saddles.

sentences.zh: 蓋輅黃絹大蒙帕一，黃油絹帕一。

translations.literal: Canopy palanquin: one large yellow silk cover cloth, one yellow oiled silk cloth.
translations.idiomatic: For covering the palanquin there was one large yellow silk cover cloth and one yellow oiled silk cloth.

sentences.zh: 駕士平巾大袖，並青繪纻絲為之。

translations.literal: Escort riders wore level kerchiefs and large sleeves, all made of green-painted ramie silk.
translations.idiomatic: The escort riders wore level kerchiefs and large sleeves, all made of green-painted ramie silk.

sentences.zh: 至治元年，英宗親祀太廟，詔中書及太常禮儀院、禮部定擬制鹵簿五輅。

translations.literal: In Zhizhi year 1, Emperor Yingzong personally sacrificed at the Imperial Ancestral Temple; an edict ordered the Secretariat and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and the Ministry of Rites to draft specifications for the five palanquins of the ceremonial guard.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizhi 1 (1321), when Emperor Yingzong personally sacrificed at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, he ordered the Secretariat, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and the Ministry of Rites to draft specifications for the five ceremonial palanquins.

sentences.zh: 以平章政事張珪、留守王伯勝、將作院使明裏董阿、侍儀使乙剌徒滿董其事。

translations.literal: Grand Councillor Zhang Gui, garrison commander Wang Bosheng, Commissioner of the Palace Construction Office Mingli Dong'a, and Master of Ceremonies Yilatuman supervised the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councillor Zhang Gui, garrison commander Wang Bosheng, Commissioner of the Palace Construction Office Mingli Dong'a, and Master of Ceremonies Yilatuman were put in charge of the work.

sentences.zh: 是年，玉輅成。

translations.literal: That year the jade palanquin was completed.
translations.idiomatic: That year the jade palanquin was completed.

sentences.zh: 明年，親祀御之。

translations.literal: The next year, at the personal sacrifice he rode it.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he rode it at his personal sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 後復命造四輅，工未成而罷。

translations.literal: Later he again ordered the making of the four palanquins; the work was not completed before it was suspended.
translations.idiomatic: Later he again ordered the construction of the four remaining palanquins, but the work was suspended before completion.

sentences.zh: 金輅。

translations.literal: Gold palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: The gold palanquin.

sentences.zh: 赤質，金妝，青綠藻井，栲栳輪蓋。

translations.literal: Red body, gold decoration, green-blue caisson ceiling, wicker-style wheel canopy.
translations.idiomatic: It had a red body with gold decoration, a green-blue caisson ceiling, and a wicker-style wheel canopy.

sentences.zh: 外施金妝雕木雲龍，內盤真金福海圓龍一，頂上匝以金塗鍮石耀葉八十一。

translations.literal: Externally applied gold-decorated carved wood cloud-dragons; internally set one solid-gold Fortune Sea round dragon; at the top encircled with eighty-one gilded brass-alloy radiant leaves.
translations.idiomatic: The exterior bore gold-decorated carved cloud-dragons in wood; within was set one round dragon of solid gold on a Fortune Sea panel; and around the apex were eighty-one gilded brass-alloy radiant leaves.

sentences.zh: 上圍九者二，中圍九者三，下圍九者四。

translations.literal: Two upper encircling nines, three middle encircling nines, four lower encircling nines.
translations.idiomatic: There were two upper rings of nine, three middle rings of nine, and four lower rings of nine.

sentences.zh: 頂輪衣三重，上二重大紅繡雲龍瑞草，下一重無文。

translations.literal: Canopy-wheel coverings in three layers; the upper two layers great-red-embroidered cloud-dragons and auspicious plants, the lower layer without pattern.
translations.idiomatic: The canopy-wheel coverings came in three layers: the upper two were embroidered in great red with cloud-dragons and auspicious plants, and the lower layer was plain.

sentences.zh: 輪衣內黃屋一，黃素纻絲瀝水，下垂朱絲結網一周，大紅纻絲繡小帶四十八，帶頭綴金塗小銅鈴三百，大紅纻絲繡絡帶二。

translations.literal: Within the wheel coverings one yellow canopy; plain yellow ramie-silk drip-water skirt; below the circumference hung a crimson-silk knotted net; forty-eight small great-red ramie-silk embroidered bands; band heads set with three hundred gilded small bronze bells; two great-red ramie-silk embroidered lacing bands.
translations.idiomatic: Within the wheel coverings was a yellow canopy with a plain yellow ramie-silk drip skirt; below hung a crimson-silk knotted net, forty-eight small great-red ramie-silk embroidered bands with three hundred gilded bronze bells at the ends, and two great-red ramie-silk embroidered lacing bands.

sentences.zh: 頂輪平素面夾用緋纻絲。

translations.literal: The canopy wheel's flat plain surface interleaved with scarlet ramie silk.
translations.idiomatic: The flat plain surface of the canopy wheel was interleaved with scarlet ramie silk.

sentences.zh: 蓋之四周垂流蘇八，飾以五色茸線結網五重，金塗鍮石雜佩八，珩璜沖瑀全，金塗鍮石鉤掛十有六，黃絨貫頂天心直下十字繩二。

translations.literal: On four sides of the canopy hung eight tassels; ornamented with five layers of five-colored plush-thread knotted net; eight gilded brass-alloy assorted pendants, complete with heng, huang, chong, and yu; sixteen gilded brass-alloy hook hangers; two yellow-plush cords running straight down from the canopy apex through the cross ropes.
translations.idiomatic: Eight tassels hung from the four sides of the canopy, which was ornamented with five layers of five-colored plush-thread knotted net, eight gilded brass-alloy pendant sets complete with heng, huang, chong, and yu ornaments, sixteen gilded brass-alloy hook hangers, and two yellow-plush cords running straight down from the canopy apex along the cross ropes.

sentences.zh: 蓋下立朱漆柱四，柱下直平盤，虛櫃，中欞三十，其下外桄二，漆繪犀、象、鸚鵡、錦雉、孔雀，隔窠嵌妝花板。

translations.literal: Below the canopy stood four vermilion-lacquer posts; below the posts a straight flat platform, hollow cabinet, thirty inner lattice bars, two outer lower rails below, lacquer-painted rhinoceros, elephant, parrot, golden pheasant, and peacock, in bordered compartments with inlaid decorative panels.
translations.idiomatic: Four vermilion-lacquer posts stood beneath the canopy; below the posts was a straight flat platform and hollow cabinet with thirty inner lattice bars and two outer lower rails below, with rhinoceroses, elephants, parrots, golden pheasants, and peacocks lacquer-painted in bordered compartments with inlaid decorative panels.

sentences.zh: 櫃上周遭朱漆勾闌，雲拱地霞葉一百七十有九，下垂牙護泥虛板，並朱漆畫瑞草。

translations.literal: Around the cabinet vermilion-lacquer balustrades, cloud-arch ground sunset-leaves one hundred seventy-nine; hanging down ivory guard mud hollow boards, all vermilion-lacquer painted auspicious plants.
translations.idiomatic: Around the cabinet ran vermilion-lacquer balustrades with one hundred seventy-nine cloud-arch and sunset-leaf ornaments; below hung ivory-edged guard panels, all painted in vermilion lacquer with auspicious plants.

sentences.zh: 勾闌上金塗鍮石行龍十二，金塗鍮石蹲龍十，孔雀羽臺九，水精面火珠七，金圈焰銅照八。

translations.literal: On the balustrades twelve gilded brass-alloy walking dragons, ten gilded brass-alloy crouching dragons, nine peacock-feather platforms, seven crystal-faced fire pearls, eight gold-ringed flame bronze mirrors.
translations.idiomatic: On the balustrades were twelve gilded brass-alloy walking dragons, ten gilded brass-alloy crouching dragons, nine peacock-feather platforms, seven crystal-faced fire pearls, and eight gold-ringed flame bronze mirrors.

sentences.zh: 輿下垂朱絲結網一遭，飾以金塗鍮石鐸子三百，彩畫鍮石梅萼嵌網眼中。

translations.literal: Around the palanquin below hung one circuit of crimson-silk knotted net, ornamented with three hundred gilded brass-alloy bells, polychrome-painted brass-alloy plum blossoms inlaid in the net eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Around the lower part of the palanquin hung one circuit of crimson-silk knotted net ornamented with three hundred gilded brass-alloy bells and polychrome-painted brass-alloy plum blossoms set into the mesh.

sentences.zh: 輿之長轅三，界轅勾心各三，上下龍頭六。

translations.literal: The palanquin had three long shafts, three boundary-shaft heart-hooks each, six dragon heads above and below.
translations.idiomatic: The palanquin had three long shafts, three boundary-shaft heart-hooks on each, and six dragon heads above and below.

sentences.zh: 前轅引手金塗鍮石螭頭三，並系以蹲龍。

translations.literal: On the front shafts three gilded brass-alloy chi-dragon hand-grips, each also tied with crouching dragons.
translations.idiomatic: On the front shafts were three gilded brass-alloy chi-dragon hand-grips, each tied with a crouching dragon.

sentences.zh: 後轅方罨頭三，桄頭十六，系以蹲龍三。

translations.literal: On the rear shafts three square yantou heads, sixteen shaft heads, tied with three crouching dragons.
translations.idiomatic: On the rear shafts were three square yantou heads and sixteen shaft heads, tied with three crouching dragons.

sentences.zh: 轅頭衡一，兩端金塗鍮石龍頭二，上列金塗銅鳳十二，含以金塗銅鈴。

translations.literal: One shaft-head crossbar, two gilded brass-alloy dragon heads at the ends, above arranged twelve gilded bronze phoenixes, holding gilded bronze bells in their beaks.
translations.idiomatic: There was one shaft-head crossbar with gilded brass-alloy dragon heads at both ends; above it stood twelve gilded bronze phoenixes holding gilded bronze bells in their beaks.

sentences.zh: 輿之軸一，輪二。

translations.literal: The palanquin had one axle, two wheels.
translations.idiomatic: The palanquin had one axle and two wheels.

sentences.zh: 軸之挲羅二，明轄蹲龍絟，並漆以赤。

translations.literal: Two axle-end collars on the axle, bright hub crouching-dragon bindings, all lacquered red.
translations.idiomatic: The axle had two end collars and bright-hub crouching-dragon bindings, all lacquered red.

sentences.zh: 輪之輻各二十有四，轂首壓貼金塗銅轂葉八十有一，金塗鍮石擎耳戀攀四。

translations.literal: Each wheel twenty-four spokes; hub cap overlaid with eighty-one gilded bronze hub leaves; four gilded brass-alloy bearing-ear love-binders.
translations.idiomatic: Each wheel had twenty-four spokes; the hub cap was overlaid with eighty-one gilded bronze hub leaves; and there were four gilded brass-alloy bearing-ear love-binders.

sentences.zh: 櫃之前，朱漆金妝雲龍輅牌一，金塗鐵曲戌。

translations.literal: Before the cabinet, one vermilion-lacquer gold-decorated cloud-dragon palanquin plaque, gilded iron curved rack.
translations.idiomatic: Before the cabinet hung one vermilion-lacquer, gold-decorated cloud-dragon palanquin plaque and a gilded iron curved rack.

sentences.zh: 輅之箱，四壁雕鎪漆畫填心隔窠龜文花板，上層左畫青龍，右畫白虎，前畫朱雀，後畫玄武。

translations.literal: The palanquin box: four walls carved, engraved, lacquer-painted, filled-center compartmented tortoise-pattern decorative panels; upper layer left painted azure dragon, right white tiger, front vermilion bird, rear dark warrior.
translations.idiomatic: The palanquin box had four walls of carved, engraved, lacquer-painted panels with filled centers, compartmented tortoise patterns, and ornamental boards; on the upper level the left side bore the azure dragon, the right the white tiger, the front the vermilion bird, and the rear the dark warrior.

sentences.zh: 輅之前額，金行龍二，奉一水精珠，後額亦如之。

translations.literal: On the palanquin front brow, two gold walking dragons, presenting one crystal pearl; the rear brow the same.
translations.idiomatic: On the front brow of the palanquin two gold walking dragons presented a crystal pearl; the rear brow was the same.

sentences.zh: 前兩柱緋絨鈴索五，貼金鸞和大響銅鈴十，金塗鍮石雙魚五。

translations.literal: On the front two posts five scarlet-plush bell cords, ten gold-appliqué luan-harmony great-sounding bronze bells, five gilded brass-alloy double fish.
translations.idiomatic: On the front two posts were five scarlet-plush bell cords, ten gold-appliqué luan-harmony great-sounding bronze bells, and five gilded brass-alloy double-fish ornaments.

sentences.zh: 下朱漆軾櫃一，櫃上金香球一，金香寶一，金香合，銀灰盤一，並黃纻絲綬帶。

translations.literal: Below one vermilion-lacquer dashboard cabinet; on the cabinet one gold incense ball, one gold incense treasure, one gold incense box, one silver ash tray, all with yellow ramie-silk cord bands.
translations.idiomatic: Below was one vermilion-lacquer dashboard cabinet bearing one each of a gold incense ball, gold incense censer, gold incense box, and silver ash tray, all with yellow ramie-silk cord bands.

sentences.zh: 輅之後，朱漆後對一，金塗曲戌，黃纻絲銷金雲龍門簾一，緋纻絲繡雲龍帶二。

translations.literal: Behind the palanquin, one vermilion-lacquer rear screen, gilded curved rack, one yellow ramie-silk cut-gold cloud-dragon door curtain, two scarlet ramie-silk embroidered cloud-dragon bands.
translations.idiomatic: Behind the palanquin stood one vermilion-lacquer rear screen and a gilded curved rack, with one yellow ramie-silk cut-gold cloud-dragon door curtain and two scarlet ramie-silk embroidered cloud-dragon bands.

sentences.zh: 輅之中，黃金妝鉸龍椅一，靠背上金塗圈焰玉明珠一。

translations.literal: Within the palanquin, one gold-decorated hinged dragon chair; on the backrest one gilded ring-flame jade bright pearl.
translations.idiomatic: Within the palanquin was one gold-decorated hinged dragon chair with a gilded ring-flame jade bright pearl on the backrest.

sentences.zh: 左建太常斿，十有二斿，緋羅繡日、月、五星、升龍。

translations.idiomatic: On the left was erected the Grand Constant streamers with twelve streamers of scarlet gauze embroidered with the sun, moon, five stars, and an ascending dragon.

sentences.zh: 右建阘戟一，九斿，緋羅繡雲龍。

translations.idiomatic: On the right was erected one tae halberd with nine streamers of scarlet gauze embroidered with cloud-dragons.

translations.literal: At the center two yellow gauze flags embroidered with green-black fu pattern, silk-cord poles, all great-red gauze.
translations.idiomatic: At the center were two yellow gauze flags embroidered with green-black fu patterns on silk-cord poles, all of great-red gauze.

translations.literal: Flag heads with two gilded brass-alloy dragon heads, two gilded bronze bells, twelve layers of gilded brass-alloy cymbal crimson tassels and cords, twelve layers of gilded wood-bead tassels.

sentences.zh: 輅之前額，白檀行龍二，奉一水精珠，後額如之。

translations.idiomatic: Within the palanquin was one gold-decorated hinged white-sandalwood carved dragon chair with a gilded ring-flame jade bright pearl on the backrest.

translations.idiomatic: On the right was erected one Grand Constant flag with twelve streamers of white gauze embroidered with the sun, moon, five stars, and an ascending dragon.

sentences.zh: 右建阘戟一，九斿，素白羅繡雲龍。

translations.literal: On the right erected one tae halberd, nine streamers, plain white gauze embroidered cloud-dragon.
translations.idiomatic: On the right was erected one tae halberd with nine streamers of plain white gauze embroidered with cloud-dragons.

translations.idiomatic: Within the balustrade were five layers of ke-tie strip mats.

sentences.zh: 輅馬、誕馬，皆白色。

sentences.zh: 誕馬白織金纻絲屜四副，白羅銷金白絹裏籠鞍六。

sentences.zh: 蓋輅黃絹大蒙帕一，黃油絹帕一。

translations.literal: Escort riders wore level kerchiefs and large sleeves, all made of white-embroidered ramie silk.
translations.idiomatic: The escort riders wore level kerchiefs and large sleeves, all made of white-embroidered ramie silk.

translations.idiomatic: The wood palanquin.

sentences.zh: 上圍九者二，中圍九者三，下圍九者四。

translations.literal: Two upper encircling nines, three middle encircling nines, four lower encircling nines.
translations.idiomatic: There were two upper rings of nine, three middle rings of nine, and four lower rings of nine.

sentences.zh: 頂輪衣三重，上二重皂繡雲龍瑞草，下一重無文。

translations.literal: Canopy-wheel coverings in three layers; the upper two layers black-embroidered cloud-dragons and auspicious plants, the lower layer without pattern.

sentences.zh: 頂輪平素面夾用檀褐纻絲。

translations.literal: The canopy wheel's flat plain surface interleaved with sandalwood-brown ramie silk.
translations.idiomatic: The flat plain surface of the canopy wheel was interleaved with sandalwood-brown ramie silk.

translations.idiomatic: Saddles, bridles, cruppers, girths, tassels, whisk-feathers, and neck collars were all of light black leather with gold decoration.

sentences.zh: 誕馬紫織金纻絲屜四副，紫羅銷金紫絹裏籠鞍六。

translations.literal: Attendant horses: four sets purple woven-gold ramie-silk shin guards, six purple gauze cut-gold purple-silk-lined cage saddles.
translations.idiomatic: The attendant horses had four sets of purple woven-gold ramie-silk shin guards and six purple gauze cut-gold purple-silk-lined cage saddles.

sentences.zh: 蓋輅黃絹大蒙帕一，黃油絹帕一。

translations.literal: Canopy palanquin: one large yellow silk cover cloth, one yellow oiled silk cloth.
translations.idiomatic: For covering the palanquin there was one large yellow silk cover cloth and one yellow oiled silk cloth.

sentences.zh: 駕士平巾大袖，皆紫繡纻絲為之。

translations.literal: Escort riders wore level kerchiefs and large sleeves, all made of purple-embroidered ramie silk.
translations.idiomatic: The escort riders wore level kerchiefs and large sleeves, all made of purple-embroidered ramie silk.

sentences.zh: 腰輿。

translations.literal: Waist litter.
translations.idiomatic: The waist litter.

sentences.zh: 制以香木，後背作山字牙，嵌七寶妝雲龍屏風，上施金圈焰明珠，兩傍引手。

translations.literal: Made of fragrant wood; the backrest formed mountain-character teeth; inlaid seven-jewel-decorated cloud-dragon screen; above applied gold ring-flame bright pearl; hand-grips on both sides.
translations.idiomatic: It was made of fragrant wood, with a backrest shaped in mountain-character teeth, an inlaid cloud-dragon screen decorated with the seven jewels, a gold ring-flame bright pearl mounted above, and hand-grips on both sides.

sentences.zh: 屏風下施雕鏤雲龍床。

translations.literal: Below the screen was fitted a carved openwork cloud-dragon bed.
translations.idiomatic: Below the screen was fitted a carved openwork cloud-dragon couch.

sentences.zh: 坐前有踏床，可貼錦褥一。

translations.literal: Before the seat a foot-rest; one ke-tie brocade cushion.
translations.idiomatic: Before the seat was a foot-rest and one ke-tie brocade cushion.

sentences.zh: 坐上貂鼠緣金錦條褥，綠可貼方坐。

translations.literal: On the seat a sable-bordered gold-brocade strip mat, green ke-tie square seat.
translations.idiomatic: On the seat were a sable-bordered gold-brocade strip mat and a green ke-tie square seat.

sentences.zh: 象轎。

translations.literal: Elephant palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: The elephant palanquin.

sentences.zh: 駕以象，凡巡幸則御之。

translations.literal: Drawn by elephants; whenever the ruler went on inspection tours, he rode it.
translations.idiomatic: It was drawn by elephants; on inspection tours the ruler rode it.
